headline: Bangladesh crushes Australia by nine wickets for historic first-ever Test win on Australian soil
summary: The Tigers made history in Darwin, becoming the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, securing a dominant victory on Day 4.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic milestone in Darwin, defeating Australia by nine wickets on Sunday for their first-ever Test win on Australian soil. After bowling the hosts out for 284, Bangladesh needed just 57 runs and comfortably reached the target in the second session on Day 4.

This victory makes Bangladesh the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, accomplishing it in their third Test Down Under. This record surpasses Pakistan (7 Tests) and India (12 Tests), while Sri Lanka remains winless after 15 attempts.

Only England won their first Test in Australia sooner, in their second Test on Australian soil, which was also only the second Test in history. South Africa also secured a win in Australia in their third Test.

Bangladesh's nine-wicket triumph is their second-biggest Test victory by wickets, following their 10-wicket win over Pakistan in Rawalpindi in 2024. It marks only their second win against Australia in seven Tests, with the first being in Mirpur in 2017.

This loss is Australia's first home Test defeat to an Asian team other than India in 31 years, dating back to 1995. It is also Bangladesh's second Test win in SENA (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia) countries, after their notable victory over New Zealand in Mount Maunganui in 2022.

Individual performances were key, with Hasan Mahmud's match figures of 9-111 being the second-best by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests. These figures are also the best by a Bangladesh bowler outside the country. Tanzid Tamim became the sixth Bangladesh player to score a century and a duck in the same Test.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto recorded his third away Test win, the most by any Bangladesh captain, surpassing Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim. Shanto now holds the record for most Test wins as Bangladesh captain, with nine.
The Darwin Test also saw a record attendance of 18,352 fans, marking the highest-ever Test attendance at the venue, reflecting the excitement around this historic match.

topic: Bangladesh power gas crisis fix timeline
headline_marked: [[Minimum two years needed to fix power, gas crisis]], says Finance Minister Khosru
headline: Minimum two years needed to fix power, gas crisis, says Finance Minister Khosru
summary: Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury stated that Bangladesh faces significant inherited infrastructure problems in its power and gas sectors. The government is actively working on solutions, but full resolution will take time.
details: It will take at least two years to fully resolve Bangladesh’s ongoing power and gas shortages, according to Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury. He made this statement at an event organized by the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) in Dhaka.

The minister acknowledged that the government inherited major infrastructure problems within these sectors. He assured that efforts are underway to address these issues as quickly as possible, emphasizing that no moment is being wasted.

Regarding gas supply, Khosru mentioned that decisions on floating liquefied natural gas terminals and onshore storage facilities are being finalized. These plans are expected to be announced within the next few days.

He also highlighted that while Bangladesh has the capacity to generate substantial electricity, inadequate transmission capacity poses a significant challenge. The government is reviewing its power generation policy and energy mix, aiming for an integrated approach including renewables and gas.

Deregulation is another key priority in the current budget, despite the challenges of implementation in a highly regulated country. A task force has been formed, and a website launched for businesses and citizens to report bureaucratic obstacles.

On taxation, the government is tackling longstanding corruption and harassment. It plans to separate tax policy-making from administration at the National Board of Revenue, with an expert group developing policies and a move towards full automation.

The banking sector also requires urgent attention due to severe capital shortages and high levels of non-performing loans. This has led to difficulties for depositors and businesses, prompting the government to explore a combination of state support and foreign fund management for stabilization.

AmCham President Syed Mohammad Kamal noted that American companies have invested approximately $5 billion in Bangladesh over the past two decades. AmCham members aim to invest another $5 billion in the next four to five years.

Kamal identified advanced manufacturing, the digital economy, AI, cybersecurity, healthcare, and renewable energy as high-potential sectors. He stressed that consistent implementation of reforms is crucial to translate Bangladesh’s potential into lasting investor confidence and actual investment.
